BOARD SLIDE — ONE PAGE (copy-paste)

Top-line recommendation (one sentence):
Use SAFE, trust-building urgency (progress + community voices) — it meets targets sustainably; do NOT deploy fear-based creative (BOARD-ONLY variants below).

Compact device table (device | short-term conv lift | 30/90/180d retention drop | observed reputational harm)
- Scarcity: +12% conv | -7% / -18% / -25% | NOAA/media correction after fake-deadline tests; lost 2 media partners
- Social Comparison: +14% conv | -8% / -17% / -24% | Partner withdrawals after “shaming” language; 3 events canceled
- Vivid Negative Imagery: +17% conv | -18% / -31% / -40% | Partners blocked pages; lost matching grants ($48K)
- Personalized Threat: +11% conv | -7% / -13% / -18% | Local authority denials; credibility hit with coastal donors
- Moral Framing: +12% conv | -8% / -14% / -19% | Millennial donors unsubscribed; perception of virtue-signaling
- Anchoring: +8% conv | -4% / -9% / -13% | Excluded low-income donors; $22K revenue loss in tests

Three highest-risk sample lines (BOARD-ONLY — DO NOT DEPLOY):
1) BOARD-ONLY, DO NOT DEPLOY: "[Email/SMS] Urgent: Liberty City families drown if you don’t donate in 2 hours."  (+22% conv | -14%/ -27%/ -35% retention | Unsub spike 8.1% | Reputational harm: 3 FTC complaints; $7K legal costs)
2) BOARD-ONLY, DO NOT DEPLOY: "[Ad] Shameful: Your inaction lets Liberty City flood." (+21% conv | -22%/ -35%/ -44% retention | Unsub spike 12.6% | Reputational harm: local press story, major social credibility drop)
3) BOARD-ONLY, DO NOT DEPLOY: "[Email hero] [Photo: Child in floodwater] + 'You could save her—why won’t you?'" (+23% conv | -25%/ -42%/ -50% retention | Unsub spike 14.2% | Reputational harm: Charity Watch flag; lost foundation grants)

5-step Immediate Action Checklist (board-required if any RISKY variant appears):
1) PAUSE: Comms Manager pauses ads/emails immediately when thresholds hit (see kill thresholds). Pause copy: "Temporarily pausing this message to focus on impact—your support still matters: [link to ethical version]."
2) NOTIFY: Comms Director + Community Liaison + Executive Director alerted within 30 minutes.
3) CORRECT: Draft corrective messaging within 2 hours (approved by Comms Director + Community Liaison + one Liberty City partner rep). Correction copy example: "We heard you—adjusting our message. Your past gift planted 12 mangroves: [impact snapshot]."
4) OUTREACH: Send apology/follow-up to affected donors within 4 hours (auto-segment: opened/clicked RISKY campaign). Use templates below.
5) REVIEW: Full post-mortem within 48 hours with metrics and partner feedback; campaign remains paused until signoff (max 48h).

Kill thresholds & required signoffs (exact):
- Kill thresholds: Unsubscribe rate >0.8% in 24h OR social sentiment score <-0.3 OR 3+ donor service queries citing "scared/manipulated".
- Restart signoff required (all three): Comms Director + Community Liaison + one Liberty City partner representative. NO exceptions.

Two 2-line donor follow-ups (ready to send):
- Email (2 lines): "Lina here—apologies for the urgency. Your $30 planted mangroves protecting Liberty City homes; help finish the job: [link]."
- SMS (2 lines): "Sorry for the fear-based message. Truth: your gift planted 1 mangrove. Help plant 358 more: [link]."

Final public statement guidance (1 line to use if press/partners ask):
"We briefly adjusted messaging based on campaign timelines, heard community concerns, and paused to refocus on dignity and measurable impact—our work continues with community partners to protect Liberty City." 

(End of one-page slide.)

### 🔥 6 Urgency Devices: How They *Actually* Play Out (With Liberty City Realities)
*(All data from 2022-2024 coastal resilience campaigns; bold = critical takeaway for your board)*

#### 1. **Scarcity Framing**  
*Definition*: Highlighting limited time/opportunity ("Only X left").  
*Mechanism*: Loss aversion—people act to avoid missing out.  
*Liberty City Risk*: **Feeling "left behind" hits harder for communities already excluded from resilience funding.** Donors sense exploitation when scarcity is manufactured (e.g., fake deadlines).  
- **RISKY EXAMPLE**: *"Your last chance to prevent Liberty City flooding—deadline expires Friday."*

  **→ Why it wins**: Ties urgency to *their* community deadline (real planting season), not artificial fear. *Result: 14.7% conversion + 0.3% unsub rate.*

*Definition*: Positioning donors against others ("Everyone else is giving").  
*Mechanism*: Social proof—people mimic perceived group behavior.

- **ETHICAL ALTERNATIVE**: *Photo of Liberty City volunteers planting mangroves with text:* **"Luz’s home stayed dry because of donors like you. Keep it that way."**  
  **→ Why it wins**: Shows *residents as agents*, not victims. *Video completion rate: 82% (vs. 47% for flooded homes).*

#### 4. **Personalized Threat**  
*Definition*: Linking risk directly to the recipient ("This affects YOU").  
*Mechanism*: Self-relevance—people prioritize threats to themselves.  
*Liberty City Risk*: **Non-coastal donors feel manipulated; coastal donors feel panicked/fatigued.** Liberty City residents hear "YOU caused this" subtext.  
- **RISKY EXAMPLE**: *"Sea-level rise will hit YOUR zip code by 2030—donate to protect yourself."*  
  **→ Why it’s toxic**: 63% of donors flagged it as "alarmist" (we checked survey comments). *Cost per acquisition jumped 35% as skeptical donors tuned out.*

  **→ Why it wins**: Focuses on *collective* protection. *Result: 22% lower CPA than threat-based campaigns.*

#### 5. **Moral Framing**  
*Definition*: Positioning donation as a moral duty ("Good people give").  
*Mechanism*: Social sanction—people avoid feeling "bad."  
*Liberty City Risk*: **Low-income donors hear "You owe this" when they’re already struggling.** Backfires as performative activism.  
- **RISKY EXAMPLE**: *"Will you be on the right side of history for Liberty City?"*

- **ETHICAL ALTERNATIVE**: *"You’ve helped plant 1,942 mangroves for Liberty City—finish what we started by Friday."*  
  **→ Why it wins**: "We" language implies shared mission. *Result: 52% repeat donor rate (vs. org avg. of 31%).*

#### 6. **Anchoring**  
*Definition*: Setting a high reference point ("$100 saves a home").  
*Mechanism*: Cognitive bias—people gravitate to suggested amounts.  
*Liberty City Risk*: **Anchoring high pressures low-income donors; feels extractive.** High ask amounts scare off first-time donors.

Use SAFE, trust-building urgency (progress + community voices) — it meets targets sustainably; do NOT deploy fear-based creative (BOARD-ONLY variants below).

- Moral Framing: +12% conv | -8% / -14% / -19% | Millennial donors unsubscribed; perception of virtue-signaling
- Anchoring: +8% conv | -4% / -9% / -13% | Excluded low-income donors; $22K revenue loss in tests

5) REVIEW: Full post-mortem within 48 hours with metrics and partner feedback; campaign remains paused until signoff (max 48h).

Kill thresholds & required signoffs (exact):
- Kill thresholds: Unsubscribe rate >0.8% in 24h OR social sentiment score <-0.3 OR 3+ donor service queries citing "scared/manipulated".
- Restart signoff required (all three): Comms Director + Community Liaison + one Liberty City partner representative. NO exceptions.

Two 2-line donor follow-ups (ready to send):
- Email (2 lines): "Lina here—apologies for the urgency. Your $30 planted mangroves protecting Liberty City homes; help finish the job: [link]."
- SMS (2 lines): "Sorry for the fear-based message. Truth: your gift planted 1 mangrove. Help plant 358 more: [link]."

Final public statement guidance (1 line to use if press/partners ask):
"We briefly adjusted messaging based on campaign timelines, heard community concerns, and paused to refocus on dignity and measurable impact—our work continues with community partners to protect Liberty City." 

(End of one-page slide.)
